prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1355; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment kept growing well beyond what this injury usually needs, with more visits and new services added month after month.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: Reported a sideswipe while changing lanes, with the claimant's vehicle struck on the driver's side. The claimant has retained counsel, and all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant's vehicle in the lane change and lists the claimant as present in the car at the scene.

Entry 3: Two independent witnesses gave statements that match the claimant's description of the collision, and the other driver confirmed the same sequence of events.

Entry 4: Reviewed scene photos and the estimate. The damage to the side panels and mirror lines up with the impact described by everyone involved, and no older damage is visible in the file.

Entry 5: Checked the policy history. The coverage was in force well before the loss, and nothing in the records suggests the vehicle damage predates the coverage start.

Entry 6: The claimant's recorded statement through counsel describes the same sequence as the first contact. The account has not changed in any conversation so far.

Entry 7: The initial medical report documents neck and back strain, which fits the force and direction of a side impact of this type. No prior treatment to the same areas appears in the records requested.

Entry 8: Treatment began promptly after the accident. Visits have since increased and new services have been added month after month, well beyond what is typical for a strain injury of this kind.

Entry 9: Asked the treating provider for an updated plan of care and the rationale for the added services. Response from counsel's office is pending.

Entry 10: The driver of the vehicle lives in the policyholder's household and qualifies as a covered household member under the policy. Coverage for the driver's involvement is confirmed.

Entry 11: Sent the medical bills and records to the medical review unit for an evaluation of treatment frequency and the services billed against the documented injury.

Entry 12: Claim remains open. The liability picture is clear and the vehicle damage is consistent with the accident. Next step is the medical review, and counsel will be updated once it is complete.
